methods.notes: VESC Express advertises the Nordic UART service; the name is user-set. Confirm with a COMM_FW_VERSION (id 0) exchange.

device.name: VESC (open-source motor controller)
device.notes:
VESC is the open-source motor-controller firmware (bldc) that powers a huge number of DIY e-skateboards, EUCs and scooters, plus the VESC Express BLE add-on. The COMM packet protocol and the BLE bridge are the vendor's own open-source project — nothing was reverse-engineered.
BLE (VESC Express) uses the Nordic UART Service: service 6e400001-b5a3-f393-e0a9-e50e24dcca9e, RX/write 6e400002-..., TX/notify 6e400003-... (the same NUS UUIDs as the M365 family, so generic NUS tooling works). The advertised BLE name is configurable; the same COMM payload runs over UART too.
COMM PACKET FRAMING (comm/packet.c): start byte 0x02 (payload <=255, 1-byte length), 0x03 (<=65535, 2-byte length), 0x04 (>65535, 3-byte length); then the payload; then a 2-byte big-endian CRC16 over the payload; then stop byte 0x03. Short form: 02 | LEN | PAYLOAD | CRC_HI | CRC_LO | 03. Zero-length payloads are rejected.
COMM_PACKET_ID (datatypes.h): COMM_FW_VERSION 0, COMM_GET_VALUES 4, COMM_SET_DUTY 5, COMM_SET_CURRENT 6, COMM_SET_CURRENT_BRAKE 7, COMM_SET_RPM 8, COMM_SET_POS 9, COMM_REBOOT 29, COMM_ALIVE 30, COMM_FORWARD_CAN 34 (relay a packet to another VESC over CAN), up to COMM_MOTOR_ESTOP 159. GET_VALUES (4) returns the live telemetry block (voltage/current/RPM/duty/temps).
SAFETY: the COMM/BLE channel has NO authentication by design — anyone in BLE range who knows the protocol can command duty/current/RPM. Restrict BLE range / set a BLE PIN at the vehicle-integrator level.

openness.notes: Fully open: firmware, protocol and BLE bridge are the project's own source. Upstream is authoritative; this file normalises the published protocol.

pairing.notes: The BLE bridge is a stock Nordic UART service and pairs with nothing. This is open-source firmware rather than a reverse-engineered product, so the answer here is the project's design rather than an observation.

pin.notes: VESC Express exposes an optional PIN alongside the configurable BLE name. It is off unless the owner set it, so a client must handle both cases; where it is set it gates the COMM packet layer, not the connection.

credentials.notes: The COMM/BLE channel is unauthenticated by default (an optional BLE PIN exists in VESC Express). No Wi-Fi on the base controller. SAFETY: commands drive a motor — treat set-duty/current/RPM as advanced.

factory_reset.description:
The interesting part is the hardware route, because it is the one that works when nothing else does. From firmware 7.00 a VESC can be reset by shorting SWCLK to Hall 2 and then booting it — no USB, no CAN, no working configuration required. That is the recovery path for a controller whose settings have made it unreachable, which on open-source motor firmware is a state people do reach.
Ordinary resets are done from VESC Tool over USB or BLE against a controller that still answers.
Safety: this is a motor controller. After a reset the parameters that limit current and voltage are back at defaults that may not suit the motor or battery attached to it. Detect and configure before riding.
factory_reset.effect: Restores the motor configuration and the app configuration to firmware defaults and erases any scripts loaded onto the controller. A VESC that has been reset will not drive a motor safely until it has been configured and its motor detected again.

procedures.basis: VESC project documentation for firmware 7.00 and later, where this is given as the recovery route when USB and CAN are unavailable. Not performed here.
procedures.name: Hardware reset: short SWCLK to Hall 2 and boot

steps.action: With the controller unpowered, connect SWCLK to Hall 2.

steps.expect: Motor and app configuration return to defaults and scripts are erased.

steps.action: Remove the link, then re-detect the motor and reconfigure before applying power to a load.

methods.description: Connect to the VESC Express NUS device, subscribe to 6e400003, and write COMM packets to 6e400002 (e.g. COMM_GET_VALUES id 4 for telemetry, COMM_SET_CURRENT id 6 to command current).

steps.action: Connect and subscribe to the TX characteristic (6e400003).
Write a COMM_GET_VALUES (id 4) packet to 6e400002 and parse the telemetry reply.

setup.notes: Flash/configure via VESC Tool over USB or BLE; the BLE name and an optional PIN are configurable in VESC Express. For control, connect, subscribe to the TX characteristic, and write COMM packets to RX.

rejoin.notes: No network membership; a new BLE client connects independently.

testing.notes: Not driven against hardware by this project. The COMM packet framing and command ids are from vedderb/bldc (comm/packet.c, datatypes.h); the BLE Nordic-UART UUIDs from vedderb/vesc_express (comm_ble.c).

services.name: Nordic UART (VESC Express)
services.notes: Carries COMM packets. Write to 6e400002, read notifications on 6e400003. Framing: 02/03/04 start, length, payload, CRC16 (big-endian), 0x03 stop.
